newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Thousands of Albanians gather for pro-govt rally.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Albanians gather for pro-govt rally.

text.p: Thousands of Albanians gathered on Tuesday for a rally called by the ruling Democratic Party to denounce a wave of violence that has swept the country after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Eyewitnesses said up to 6,000 people, many chanting pro-government slogans, filled Tirana's central Skanderbeg Square, where President Sali Berisha was due to address the crowd.

Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, who was attacked by an angry mob in the southern town of Lushnje last Saturday, kicked off Tuesday's rally by laying a symbolic paving stone in Tirana's main square, which was itself the scene of weekend rioting.
The crowd, which appeared good natured and peaceful chanted "Long live Berisha".
Berisha, who assumed special powers on Sunday to send in troops to restore order around the country, was due to make his first public appearance since the unrest.

The pro-government rally was originally meant to be held in front of the headquarters of the opposition Socialist party, which the government has accused of inciting the protests. But the organisers switched the site late on Monday, saying they wanted "a constructive rally against violence and destruction".
